name: Haaland Hall
use: Medium residence hall (236 students), first-year and upper-division; Environmental Sustainability learning community
style: Neo-traditional brick residence hall with cast-stone bands and gabled roofs (from photos)

facts.text: Built as SERC C (Southeast Residence Complex), opened 2008; renamed Haaland Hall on October 11, 2013.

SERC was a three-building complex for 730 students built by Harvey Construction to designs by JSA, Inc.; SERC C is about 64,000 sq ft. Harvey first demolished nine existing two-storey buildings on the site; Phase 1 (A and B) finished by summer 2007, Phase 2 (C) by summer 2008.
Housing lists 236 students; 28 traditional doubles, 8 traditional singles and 41 suites of two doubles; some lounges converted to expanded-occupancy rooms.
Air conditioning, elevator, limited-use bathrooms on two floors, kitchen, laundry, two academic classrooms, study space and a volleyball court.
Hosts the Environmental Sustainability first-year learning community; many residents are engineering and life-science students near Kingsbury Hall.
Named for Gordon A. Haaland, UNH president 1983-90.

verdict: 2008 neo-traditional SERC hall with A/C and an elevator; comfortable but generic, with block-walled rooms.
notes: No licensed photo found. Reference exterior: brick with cast-stone bands, gabled ends, wide stair approach; tidy but generic. Room photo (shared across SERC pages): painted block walls, checkerboard vinyl tile, one double-hung window; utilitarian. Old row said "expanded occupancy in converted lounges"; Housing confirms counts exclude such spaces. No specific reviews found.
